title: Original photographic turf albedo for Glessner House v4
method: Built-in image generation; generic original material created from a text prompt. No reference photograph pixels supplied or sampled.
prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: original seamless PBR diffuse/albedo texture for the mown courtyard lawn in a historically reconstructed architectural 3D model.
Primary request: a straight-down orthographic macro photograph of a 40 cm by 40 cm patch of dense, short, finely bladed cool-season lawn, suitable for seamless tiling on real geometry. Razor-sharp natural individual 1-3 mm wide blades and small flattened cut ends, a little sparse fine tan thatch and dark soil visible between blades. Natural irregular fine growth, no broad cloudy noise.
Composition: square, entire frame filled edge to edge with grass; consistent detail density everywhere; seamless opposite edges.
Lighting: flat neutral diffuse albedo capture, evenly illuminated, no directional highlights, no large shadows, no vignette, no baked ambient-occlusion halos.
Palette: restrained natural medium olive and cool dark green, individual yellow-green tips, subtle brown thatch, no saturated neon green.
Constraints: photographic botanical detail; short maintained lawn, no tall meadow, no flowers, no stones, no leaves, no objects, no text, no border, no watermarks. This is a generic newly created material, not an image of a particular historical garden.
interpretation: Reconstructed maintained lawn material, not evidence for particular historic blades or planting.
reproducibility: Generated bitmap is preserved unchanged; numeric generator must retain it.
rights: Use, modification and redistribution with this project under LICENSE.txt; retain provenance and reconstructed confidence.
limitations: Original generated material study, not a photograph of the historic courtyard. Seamlessness and flat albedo illumination are generation targets, not measurements.
